dialogue:
Speaker2: But looking at it nationally, it's a factor that really weakens our power. Without having kids, our productivity's just gonna keep dropping.
Speaker1: Why do these idiots keep saying there’s no future for gay people when they don’t even have kids themselves?
Speaker2: I think feminists are gaslighting men and that's why society's falling apart.

Speaker1: What’s so surprising about never traveling abroad? Like it’s some impossible thing to believe?
Speaker2: Isn't it more pathetic to travel abroad just to show off when you don't even have the money?
Speaker1: I think this society really pushes the idea that if you’re not doing what everyone else is, you’re in big trouble, so it’s pretty common.
Speaker2: Honestly, I travel abroad a lot too, but I think saying it’s for experience or broadening your perspective doesn’t really hold up.

Speaker1: What’s a sinkhole, you?
Speaker2: You're clueless, it's a one-income household.
Speaker1: It's when a guy adopts and supports a girl.
Speaker2: So, no kids and you're the only one bringing in the cash.

Speaker1: There are definitely those who just throw around complicated terms to show off their knowledge without any explanation.
Speaker2: Yeah, totally. They give off a strong vibe that they're better than me.

Speaker1: I feel like kids these days won’t know Girls' Generation since they debuted in 2007.
Speaker2: I mean, if they're gonna protest, they gotta sing "Into the New World," so I bet they know it. The feminists have that song memorized like a military march.
Speaker1: I bet there are still a lot of friends who know the song but not SNSD.
Speaker2: I mean, there are still active members, so I bet people know. At least the feminists waving their lightsticks probably know who Girls' Generation is.

Speaker1: How can I deal with workplace bullying in a female-dominated company? They dump all the tough stuff on me, freak out over any little mistake, and the gossip is intense.
Speaker2: It's a chronic issue in female-dominated workplaces. Gather evidence and report it to HR, and if they don't handle it properly, switching jobs is an option too.
Speaker1: I seriously gotta think about quitting. I feel like I'm gonna lose it.
Speaker2: Yeah, can’t blame you. Taking a break and looking for a new job sounds like a good plan.
Speaker1: I’m thinking that too. If I end up back at a female-dominated company, I’ll lose it for sure.

Speaker1: They say for office workers, clothes are like armor. If you’re skilled and dress well, it can really boost your presence and open doors for success.
Speaker2: I’m basically a one-outfit guy. Can’t shake the habit from wearing a uniform, I guess?
Speaker1: I guess you can get by a bit if you dress well even without skills, but if you’ve got neither, you’re pretty much out of luck.

Speaker1: Just found out you’re the first Asian woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature. Congrats!
Speaker2: Shouldn't we think about this a bit? Do you really think a book that sold less than 10,000 copies deserves an award?
Speaker1: In 2016, "The Vegetarian" sold over 680,000 copies, and the criteria for the Nobel Prize in Literature isn't just sales.
Speaker2: What’s the point of getting a Nobel Prize that’s lost its value and authority?

Speaker1: I mean, making fun of someone for never traveling abroad is just low, you know?
Speaker2: For sure. There are always people who gotta flex no matter where they go.
Speaker1: I bet those low-key kids will be a sight to see as adults.
Speaker2: I think it shows how much the people are getting lowbrow. It's the influence of low-class capitalism.

Speaker1: I was so mad after getting teabagged in the game yesterday.
Speaker2: Sounds like some rude players! Should've taught 'em a lesson.
Speaker1: For real, teabagging's not fun or respectful! But our team won, so I felt really good.
Speaker2: Feels great, right? Getting that revenge is so satisfying.
Speaker1: I just kept following that dude since teabagging is like a greeting level.
Speaker2: Those kinds of people have probably never seen good gameplay. They’re trash both in skill and character.

Speaker1: I quit my job 'cause I just can't stand working under someone else. Can't live like this, you know?
Speaker2: I can't just live above others with my pride like this. It's driving me crazy.
Speaker1: It's a real struggle living like this after graduating from a nobody school.
Speaker2: Stop talking nonsense. Even a high school grad like me is doing fine, but if you don’t change your attitude, you’ll end up at a soup kitchen.

Speaker1: Don’t you think the fans who just accept and consume that are part of the problem too?
Speaker2: It's bad to exploit fan loyalty like that, kinda like blaming a woman for getting harassed.
Speaker1: I don’t get why people complain about it when buying an idol's album is 100% their choice, but sexual assault is 100% the criminal's fault, no matter what.
Speaker2: Are people gonna stop drinking soju just because the price went up? Fans buy albums while complaining about artists. Cut the nonsense.

Speaker1: I feel like the rise of far-right stuff is happening because old folks are getting marginalized and there's a lot of ageism.
Speaker2: For sure. Those grandpas with gas canisters or wearing Marine hats must've had a tough time raising their kids...
Speaker1: I think the problem is not acknowledging their loneliness and trying to connect with others, but rather having an attitude of hate and harm.
Speaker2: I think the far-right shift in young men is for similar reasons.

Speaker1: Why are there so many narcissists these days?
Speaker2: They're the people you gotta avoid in life.
Speaker1: It's so ironic how they can hurt others without a second thought but swear revenge for even the tiniest scratch on themselves.
Speaker2: I think "narcissist" is way too soft; they're basically just low-IQ sociopaths.

Speaker1: Some people are really pushing the whole allergy treatment thing. Modern medicine in the 21st century hasn’t solved anything beyond just easing symptoms.
Speaker2: Isn't that what they call treatment since immunotherapy desensitizes you to allergens and reduces reactions?
Speaker1: According to the FDA, there’s no allergy cure, but still so many people claim there is. This really feels like the mad cow disease republic for sure.
Speaker2: It's an FDA-approved drug, you know? Not knowing is embarrassing, but it’s not a crime. There are plenty of treatment options like sublingual therapy depending on the type of allergy.

Speaker1: We gotta change the law to punish those reckless motorcycle riders on the road.
Speaker2: I don't get how people like that even exist.
Speaker1: The government's gotta be tougher like in the U.S., but the punishment level here just isn't there.
Speaker2: I can totally see myself squished next to a homeless person on the subway in 30 years.

Speaker1: Did you see that movie yesterday?
Speaker2: Yeah, it was so deep it made me think a lot.
Speaker1: Just turn your brain off.
Speaker2: I’m thinking of checking out the interpretation and watching it again.

Speaker1: I'm worried about everything since my cousin's getting married.
Speaker2: An arranged marriage? What country are they from? As long as it’s not Southeast Asia, I’m cool with it.
Speaker1: How'd you know they're from Southeast Asia? I thought he was bringing home someone way younger, like a daughter or something.
Speaker2: Whoa, I heard he’s doing a fake marriage while leaving a husband back home, so tell your cousin to get his act together.

Speaker1: Not all Seoul universities are the same level, you know? These days, there are all kinds of ways to get in, so the quality's all over the place.
Speaker2: Yeah? But it’s a Seoul university, so there’s gotta be a lot of smart students. Maybe they just haven’t adjusted yet?
Speaker1: What are you talking about? They're barely getting in through the rural admissions because they don't meet the standards.
Speaker2: Yeah, even if they ace it in the sticks, it's tough to break out of that level.

Speaker1: I don’t get why I’m rambling like this.
Speaker2: For real. People are gonna talk no matter what, so living life my way seems like the best move.
Speaker1: True. It's my life anyway, so what do they matter?

Speaker1: Doesn't matter if it's a total mess or whatever, it doesn't apply to the unemployed at all.
Speaker2: Still, plastering's gotta be profitable, right? You know the national fund's down 80% in 5 years, 95% in 10, and gets delisted in 20, right?
Speaker1: Where are the people holding on for 50 years? That's a pointless assumption.
Speaker2: I invested in that for 40 years, and it all got delisted in the end.

Speaker1: I went on a blind date and decided I need to marry internationally.
Speaker2: Did you meet a total kimchi-soybean stew kind of girl? Gotta have a word with the matchmaker.
Speaker1: Yeah, right from the start, she was subtly looking down on people, saying guys would line up for her and all that. Total legend.
Speaker2: Ugh, I really wanna give her a smack. Guess that's the average for Korean women that age. Gotta seriously think about international marriage.

Speaker1: Isn't the media, police, and the woman who threatened him also to blame for leading to his death?
Speaker2: People like those who stir up excessive comment violence and say "who told them to die?" are also accomplices.
Speaker1: It's just ridiculous to say we shouldn't blame the police or media while mocking death.
Speaker2: Those people doing that have their own motives and reasons. They're just pathetic.

Speaker1: This whole thing just keeps getting weirder, it's giving me chills.
Speaker2: Feels like we could get a few seasons of a drama just from what’s come out so far, for real.
Speaker1: Maybe they freaked out during the interview, got exposed as a scammer, and then bolted when parents and investors started getting suspicious?
Speaker2: It's kinda funny, but I'm worried it might have a happy ending. Who knows where else they might've stashed money.

Speaker1: Lately, that Black friend of mine is going viral with girl idols for some reason.
Speaker2: It's so annoying how that guy keeps popping up in girl group videos and shorts.
Speaker1: Sometimes they push those shows in the industry because of immigration policy, you know? If there's backing, they can do multiple ones.
Speaker2: Feels like if they catch one thing, he’s done for. Seems like a lot of people are gunning for him, too.

Speaker1: Feels kinda rushed, like a love-at-first-sight thing, even with a divorce under your belt.
Speaker2: Sounds like she’s getting cozy with the new guy just like she did with Youngcheol. Bet she shared a blanket with him too.
Speaker1: Still better than that country guy from the co-op.
Speaker2: Well, whether it's divorce or remarriage, that's their choice.

Speaker1: You probably know better, right? Like, you dedicated your life or your youth or whatever...
Speaker2: I really can’t stand people who joke about repaying with a game.
Speaker1: Yeah, saying they'll repay with games just means they're making money.
Speaker2: What do they think they’re gonna repay with a game? That’s just ridiculous.
Speaker1: If you made a ton of money from baseball, at least donate something to give back.

Speaker1: Should I give my little brother some allowance even though he gets money from our parents?
Speaker2: If they’re actually helping out, then sure, but if they’re just mooching, no need to give them anything.
Speaker1: Not really doing anything, just asking for a little bit every month.
Speaker2: Sometimes I give it when I feel like it, and my brother's grateful when he gets it. But asking for it every month is kinda weird.

Speaker1: I seriously don’t get why they gotta show themselves eating that all the way in Europe.
Speaker2: I guess it's because a lot of girls think that's fun. They love spicy food, so they're the main audience, right?
Speaker1: It's kinda wild to see how proud Koreans are of spicy food when we haven't even been eating red, spicy dishes for that long historically.
Speaker2: Feeling that rush of eating Korean food while traveling abroad is totally a girl thing.

Speaker1: If there’s a married guy around, tell him not to wonder who took his wife's virginity.
Speaker2: Honestly, I just hope they didn't have an abortion.
Speaker1: Don’t get your hopes up; these days, kids have probably had an abortion at least once.
Speaker2: So, at least the girls who dated in college seem kinda clean.

Speaker1: So, you don't have to go to Burger King?
Speaker2: Not sure, thinking about skipping it.
Speaker1: If you like the people you work with, a year will fly by.
Speaker2: I'll send you the manager's number for now.

Speaker1: I blocked the guys who were being loud in the comments on my post.
Speaker2: It's kinda sad to see them freak out just trying to talk to a girl.
Speaker1: Don’t feed the basement dwellers.

Speaker1: Why should I pay for a year-end party I’m not even going to?
Speaker2: How are you supposed to attend when you're in the hospital?
Speaker1: That's what I'm saying. It's not like I'm skipping it on purpose, and they didn't even come to visit me.
Speaker2: Are those people even human?
Speaker1: They’re saying I gotta pay 'cause it was decided in a meeting, but I might as well just quit.

Speaker1: Being a working mom for 10 months now, work's manageable, but parenting after hours is still tough.
Speaker2: You’re too hard on yourself, trying to do everything perfectly. It’d be better if you just let some of it go and took it easy.
Speaker1: I really respect other working moms, doing everything alone while my daughter’s sick and I have no help.

Speaker1: Are they seriously gathering all the crazies?
Speaker2: I seriously question if that's even a fair comparison.
Speaker1: I bet that person's a 방통대 grad. No clue why they included dropping out of 서울대.
Speaker2: I'm so tired of all the nonsense people spout.

Speaker1: Those people are freaking out in the comments.
Speaker2: Is it normal to get a lighter sentence for doing drugs? Other people aren't as dumb as you.
Speaker1: The comments are just a mess. Seriously, it's like there are only ignorant people out there.
Speaker2: Why are they getting a lighter sentence when they're a repeat offender?

Speaker1: They're just pathetic losers who found my parents' address through a private investigator.
Speaker2: I can see why you'd be freaked out if your address got leaked.
Speaker1: He said the YouTuber felt relieved after getting bombarded with texts, like they’re too pathetic to do anything.
Speaker2: That could really be dangerous, right? How do we know if that person’s actually crazy?

Speaker1: What’s the point of asking in group chats or communities when you could just look it up?
Speaker2: Could be 'cause there’s a lot of ads when you search, or maybe they just wanna chat.
Speaker1: Yeah, that makes sense. They might just wanna connect with people over it.

Speaker1: I'm never dating a broke guy again. It's not just the money; the low self-esteem and insecurity are just pathetic.
Speaker2: Wow, our wife living with a broke husband is really something.
Speaker1: You don't show that side, though. You're really kind and caring.
Speaker2: Money isn't everything. You can have it one day and be broke the next.
Speaker1: But low self-esteem formed during times of being broke can't be fixed even with money.

Speaker1: I've been hearing those show doctors on TV talking about stuff like accelerated aging and slow aging a lot lately.
Speaker2: That doctor looks like they’re aging twice as fast, so I’m not buying it.
Speaker1: I think the stuff that keeps popping up on TV is just fear marketing to sell more and squeeze money out of people.
Speaker2: Especially that person seems super untrustworthy. The way they talk about aging, they look the oldest themselves.

Speaker1: It's crazy that it only took 10 years to ruin 61 lives.
Speaker2: The main culprit gets 10 years and the rest only 4? The law's really lacking. Those people will be out in no time to do it again.
Speaker1: It's wild that the victims from Seoul National University had to catch the guy themselves while the police just gave up. This country lets them out after like 2 years, too.
Speaker2: In another country, they would’ve gotten 610 years. This makes me think the police and judges are all just irresponsible.

Speaker1: If you cared that much about the cat, you could’ve visited your parents more often or found it a good home.
Speaker2: You knew I was a cat mom before we got married, though.
Speaker1: Do you really think it makes sense to choose a cat over your own kid?
Speaker2: I think cat moms tend to prioritize cats over people because they're infected with toxoplasmosis; it's just how it is.

Speaker1: Any chill side gigs out there?
Speaker2: Seriously? You say that to me, who's grinding day and night? Do you even have a conscience?
Speaker1: Don’t live like that. You gotta travel and enjoy while you’re healthy. Don’t wanna regret it when you’re old.
Speaker2: Don't worry, I'll live it up while I watch you homeless with all your limbs intact.

Speaker1: Sounds like they think their genes are superior or something.
Speaker2: Why do mother-in-laws always say stuff like that?
Speaker1: They're trying to cut ties by saying they can't show a nonexistent baby.
Speaker2: It's really upsetting that they can't express themselves any better at their age.

Speaker1: Seems like the new hires are getting lazier and less motivated.
Speaker2: They've got the degrees, but they're short on experience and patience.
Speaker1: Seems like effort and grit are a thing of the past now.
Speaker2: I guess I gotta lower my expectations to feel better.

Speaker1: You know I really care about you, right?
Speaker2: What are you talking about? You drunk?
Speaker1: Always sorry and grateful.
Speaker2: Just stop and go to sleep.

Speaker1: I really think this got pushed back because of looks.
Speaker2: What do you mean "behind"? You got those doll eyes, right?
Speaker1: It's frustrating, not saying I'm uglier, just that I got outmatched in looks. Isn't social life tough?
Speaker2: Whoever's looking can see they're way better, are you blind?

Speaker1: Whoa, what’s happening? First snow and I’m stuck on the road. It’s been 2 hours already.
Speaker2: I was stuck in traffic too, cars lined up everywhere.
Speaker1: I don't get what they're doing when this crazy weather keeps happening with no prep.
Speaker2: I'm more worried since it's an electric car. No snow chains either. Might as well just park it and wait.
Speaker1: Guess I should do that. Better to just go to sleep instead of waiting.

Speaker1: I have trauma from that person.
Speaker2: What are you talking about? How'd that person give you trauma?
Speaker1: So, when I was really into OjiCom, the first people I met said they thought I’d like that guy.
Speaker2: That's hilarious.

Speaker1: Sounds like if they get sued like that, they won't be pulling that kind of stuff anymore.
Speaker2: That's true. In that situation, killing's way better. You just do a few years for murder and it's over.
Speaker1: If you try to settle for a few million won to avoid prison, you end up losing the money and still being a sex offender, so you can't do anything anyway.
Speaker2: If I get involved with a Korean girl, it feels like one of us is gonna end up dead.

Speaker1: When are you gonna stop holding the students back with all this Dongduk University mockery?
Speaker2: Yo Dongduk, stop talking and just pay back the school.
Speaker1: Yo, Donghyun's here again, can you just leave?
Speaker2: Running away and telling me to shut up when you’ve got nothing to say? Classic feminism, huh?

Speaker1: The smell from the guy next to me is really strong.
Speaker2: How about gifting some air freshener or deodorizer?
Speaker1: I tried that already, but it didn’t help. Just breathing makes me wanna gag.
Speaker2: Gotta be honest about it. Switching seats could work too.
Speaker1: Work's fun, but this unexpected issue's got me stressed.

Speaker1: There are way too many people who just start arguing during pressure interviews.
Speaker2: They're just trying to weed out the ones who bail at the first sign of criticism.
Speaker1: That's why your company isn't growing, with that old-school mindset.
Speaker2: Seems like if you poke at the kids these days, their true colors show. Handling the MZ generation feels easier than dealing with elementary schoolers.

Speaker1: You could get sued for stuff like that if you order food overseas the way we do here.
Speaker2: Companies wanna go global, but they're stuck because of weak regulations.
Speaker1: What are you talking about? I just heard a Korean CEO in the U.S. got sued for being a jerk and got hit with a huge fine!
Speaker2: Are you one of those woke lefties?

Speaker1: If you're going through menopause, just own it. Why are you flipping the AC on and off like it's a big deal?
Speaker2: Might wanna quit and go see the grandkids instead.

Speaker1: I really don’t want anyone telling me if someone’s talking trash about me. It’s so gross when they act like they care and then pass it on.
Speaker2: They're just telling you 'cause they like you, it's not that gross. Aren't you overthinking it a bit?
Speaker1: They're just telling me for their own amusement, like if I get mad I'm petty, and if I'm blank-faced I'm fake.
Speaker2: Don't think so negatively.

Speaker1: Is that even a thing?
Speaker2: Why do they keep helping people who don’t really contribute to the country’s budget?
Speaker1: If we keep coddling them, they'll get used to living off handouts.
Speaker2: I guess the government thinks forgiving debt and letting those people just get by is good enough.
Speaker1: I'm really pissed off. It's making me not wanna work.

Speaker1: In a world where school authority is weak, it's only natural for parents to hire private investigators for personal retribution when bullying happens.
Speaker2: Those bullies are a real problem. They're definitely a menace to society, and we gotta get rid of them.
Speaker1: I'd rather go to jail than have my kid jump off the apartment roof.
Speaker2: Since the weak get bullied, hiring someone really strong to shut them up will totally keep them away.

Speaker1: Going to the recycling bin in our apartment seriously makes me sigh.
Speaker2: Seems like there are a lot of people with issues, so nothing's changing.
Speaker1: Isn't it common sense to remove all the tape before throwing away delivery boxes?
Speaker2: That's nothing. There are tons of people who just toss leftover takeout.
Speaker1: I don’t get who’s supposed to clean that up. Humanity’s really hit rock bottom.

Speaker1: Seems like that person’s been at it for 10 years but still can’t handle the job right.
Speaker2: So they're just collecting a paycheck, huh?
Speaker1: He's just cycling through subordinates to keep his spot without earning it.
Speaker2: I've seen some people get promoted and start slacking off more than before.

Speaker1: Who is this person on Masked Singer? At this point, it feels like anyone can show up.
Speaker2: Just reading the subtitles feels like I can smell blood.
Speaker1: Looks like they’d mix steroids into whatever drink the members are having.
Speaker2: Guess there really aren’t any stars these days, now we’ve got regular folks coming out.

Speaker1: My friend thinks it's lame how people gawk at others' love lives.
Speaker2: It's full of people who think they're so cool but can't tell the difference between being cool and being socially awkward. Total narcissists.
Speaker1: For real. That person's self-absorption totally kills the vibe for others.
Speaker2: Best to just laugh it off and switch topics.

Speaker1: Is it true that a woman's pretty face, whether natural or from surgery, is like passing three bar exams?
Speaker2: From a guy's perspective, that's been true since the Joseon Dynasty. What have you been doing instead of studying for the exams?
Speaker1: I didn’t have time to work on my looks because I was busy studying for the exams, okay!
Speaker2: What a shame you were wasting your time on the wrong things in this day and age.
Speaker1: I'd rather make money than look attractive to a guy like you with no brain.

Speaker1: I'm really annoyed by the lady's turf war.
Speaker2: It's a shame that just because they're older, they think they deserve special treatment.
Speaker1: I wanna yank the keyboard cord and smack something.
Speaker2: It's kinda funny how you're just losing it all by yourself, huh?

Speaker1: The mom of the kid who bought the game console on Carrot Market is freaking out, asking for the account info.
Speaker2: Sounds like a full-time mom begging on Danggeun Market.
Speaker1: I flat out said no.
Speaker2: There are more people like that than you'd think. It's not just the entitled moms.

Speaker1: You know the easiest way for a girl to mess up her life?
Speaker2: What could that even be?
Speaker1: Marrying a broke guy with no social skills and having kids while you're still young.
Speaker2: Ugh, just hearing that drains me. What did the kids do to deserve this?
Speaker1: In the end, it’s a lesson to value yourself and make smart choices, right?

Speaker1: It’s really sad how many people in this country get joy from others' failures. Feels like they’re just tearing each other down.
Speaker2: It's reality that they mock even without failure, so I can't imagine how much worse it gets when you do fail. There are so many insecure people who say passing the 9th grade exam is just like being a mover or a delivery guy.
Speaker1: It seems like the obsession with comparison and money is a global thing, but it feels especially intense in Korea.
Speaker2: They just mock and leave hate comments to relieve their stress and feel superior, it's all about their own satisfaction.

Speaker1: They say Argentina just made 'Kimchi Day' a national holiday.
Speaker2: I can't believe Argentina has a Kimchi Day when we don't even have one!
Speaker1: I don't get it either. Isn't it a bit much to make it a national holiday?
Speaker2: What's the difference from designating a Tanghulu Day in our country?
Speaker1: Guess we gotta be proud if kimchi's that great.

Speaker1: Sounds like your mom didn't go to college, huh?
Speaker2: Why do people leave weird comments like this? Is it some insecurity about their school?
Speaker1: Maybe it’s better to reflect on your own shortcomings instead of blaming others? Getting into a Seoul university is tough for everyone.
Speaker2: Anyway, it seems like people with twisted personalities are the ones who comment the most.

Speaker1: They say by 2040, only national and metropolitan universities will be left.
Speaker2: Looks like colleges have no choice with freshmen dropping like that.
Speaker1: Maybe the situation up till now has been kinda abnormal. There are a lot of schools out there just cashing in without being legit foundations.
Speaker2: It could be because they’re throwing funding at those private schools, which is why public and regional universities are struggling.
Speaker1: Yeah, with the birth rate dropping, there are a ton of issues.
Speaker2: For real, how can a country survive without its people?

Speaker1: What does that comment about being fatter even mean?
Speaker2: They're just pig dads. People who think being a pig is better than being a skinny guy.
Speaker1: The styling down below is really on point.
Speaker2: They're just pretending to feel better about their chubby selves in the mirror.

Speaker1: Heard a 20-something woman got arrested by airport staff in Japan.
Speaker2: Wait, why’d she go all the way to Japan to do that?
Speaker1: Heard the airport staff stopped a girl taking pics of an idol's staff.
Speaker2: Yikes, the craziness just keeps spilling out. Fans breaking the law is beyond imagination.
Speaker1: I guess you could say a passionate Korean woman represented the country.

Speaker1: So, it’s saying it’s only gonna set gender as male or female, not including gender X.
Speaker2: I just can’t wrap my head around that identity. Feels like there’s something off mentally.
Speaker1: They should just be accepted without persecution or oppression, but trying to be mainstream is what gets them backlash.
Speaker2: This is right. Listening to people with mental issues is just messing up the country.

Speaker1: He totally covered the place with calligraphy of 'sex' from the ethics book.
Speaker2: Someone said to think of it like raising a big lizard and just let it go.
Speaker1: It's frustrating to think that I'm losing to that kid who's going through puberty while I'm in menopause.
Speaker2: Since common sense isn't gonna work, just get him some chicken. That's all you gotta do, mom.
Speaker1: I don't even wanna see him eat, why would I wanna buy him chicken?
Speaker2: They say adolescence is just a temporary mental phase. Hang in there and keep it together.

Speaker1: Classic writing from a schizophrenic.
Speaker2: It's all over the place, full of suspicion and paranoia.
Speaker1: Got no family? Seems like you need some help.
Speaker2: Seems like a really hard person to understand.

Speaker1: A lot of kids ignore their parents once they turn twenty.
Speaker2: It's kinda rough to act like that after your parents took care of you for 20 years.
Speaker1: I think age and being an adult are two different things. You gotta act your age to be a real adult.

Speaker1: I'm curious why they got rid of the arrow button on Street View and added touch functionality; it just takes me to weird places and it's annoying.
Speaker2: Guess I’m not the only one getting sent to weird places.
Speaker1: It's super frustrating trying to move around in units other than street view; it just lags.
Speaker2: I seriously wonder if they made the update annoying on purpose to push users to switch to other services.

Speaker1: Is my girlfriend saying I smell like a white guy a diss or a compliment?
Speaker2: How does your girlfriend even know what a white person smells like? She’s definitely dated one before.
Speaker1: Stop joking around, I'm being serious right now.
Speaker2: Isn't it just a mix of cheese and butter smell?
Speaker1: It’s not a stinky smell, right? Is she hinting I smell like body odor?
